scenes.visual: Title card 'Two Halves of One Lake' over a cartoon lake seen from above. COLOUR MAP, same in both films and the lesson: dashed GOLD line = the boundary; BLUE arrows = inputs crossing in; RED arrows = outputs crossing out; GREY ring of arrows = the internal loop inside the line; TEAL 'N' blocks = nitrogen; GOLD 'P' blocks = phosphorus. Cream background, 16:9. Numbers appear only as on-screen text. Valleys, trees, microbes and lakes are simple labelled cartoons marked 'schematic'; the counter values are computed from the lesson's numbers. Same colour map as the first film.

scenes.tts: Phosphorus has no major gas, so no microbe can fix it from the air. Nitrogen can be fixed by microbes. So when a lake turns green with algae, which input should you cut, nitrogen or phosphorus?
scenes.visual: Continuing from the lesson text: a cartoon lake ringed by the dashed GOLD boundary, with one BLUE input arrow carrying TEAL 'N' and one carrying GOLD 'P'. Above it a sky band labelled 'air': a dotted TEAL arrow 'N fixation' drops from the sky; a crossed-out GOLD sky arrow labelled 'P: no major gas'. The water tints green. Label: 'cut which input?'
scenes.narration: Phosphorus has no major gas, so no microbe can fix it from the air. Nitrogen can be fixed by microbes. So when a lake turns green with algae, which input should you cut, nitrogen or phosphorus?

scenes.tts: Both elements reach a lake as inputs, such as inflowing water, dust and fertiliser. Only nitrogen has a second kind of input, fixation from the air by microbes. Which one sets how much algae a lake can hold?
scenes.visual: BLUE input arrows labelled 'inflow', 'dust', 'fertiliser' carry both TEAL N and GOLD P into the lake. Then the dotted TEAL 'fixation' arrow from the sky band brightens; no GOLD arrow comes from the sky. Labels: 'P inputs: inflow, dust, fertiliser; no fixation' and 'N inputs: those routes + fixation'.
scenes.narration: Both elements reach a lake as inputs, such as inflowing water, dust and fertiliser. Only nitrogen has a second kind of input, fixation from the air by microbes. Which one sets how much algae a lake can hold?

scenes.tts: David Schindler was invited to lead whole-lake experiments in northwestern Ontario. Small lakes were set aside, so whole ecosystems could be changed and watched for years. Short tests in bottles can miss slow changes, like a rise in nitrogen fixation.
scenes.visual: Map of Canada with a pin 'Experimental Lakes Area, northwestern Ontario'. Name card 'David W. Schindler, invited 1968'. Zoom to a cluster of small cartoon lakes, two labelled '226' and '227'.
scenes.narration: David Schindler was invited to lead whole-lake experiments in northwestern Ontario. Small lakes were set aside, so whole ecosystems could be changed and watched for years. Short tests in bottles can miss slow changes, like a rise in nitrogen fixation.

scenes.tts: Lake two-twenty-six was divided by a barrier into two basins. Both basins received nitrogen, as nitrate, and carbon, as the sugar sucrose.
scenes.caption: Lake 226 was divided by a barrier into two basins. Both basins received nitrogen, as nitrate, and carbon, as the sugar sucrose.
scenes.visual: Lake 226 from above; a barrier line splits it into 'basin A' and 'basin B'. Into each, a BLUE arrow with TEAL 'N (nitrate)' and a BLUE arrow with a grey 'C (sucrose)' block.
scenes.narration: Lake 226 was divided by a barrier into two basins. Both basins received nitrogen, as nitrate, and carbon, as the sugar sucrose.

scenes.tts: One basin also received phosphorus. The other got none. So the only difference in what each half was given was that one element.
scenes.visual: A third BLUE arrow carrying GOLD 'P' enters basin B only. Basin A's label: 'N + C'; basin B's: 'N + C + P'.
scenes.narration: One basin also received phosphorus. The other got none. So the only difference in what each half was given was that one element.

scenes.tts: Both halves had plenty of nitrogen and carbon to work with. Only one had phosphorus. Which half turns green?
scenes.visual: Both basins still clear blue-grey. A question card between them: 'Which half turns green?'
scenes.narration: Both halves had plenty of nitrogen and carbon to work with. Only one had phosphorus. Which half turns green?

scenes.visual: Hold; a timer circle fills over five seconds.

scenes.tts: Only the phosphorus basin. It became highly eutrophic, rich in nutrients and dense with algae. The other basin stayed as it had been.
scenes.visual: Basin B floods bright green with cartoon algae; basin A stays clear. Label on B: 'highly eutrophic'. Small citation tag 'Schindler, Science, 1974'.
scenes.narration: Only the phosphorus basin. It became highly eutrophic, rich in nutrients and dense with algae. The other basin stayed as it had been.

scenes.tts: So in that lake, with nitrogen and carbon plentiful, phosphorus limited the algae. A nutrient is limiting when adding it on its own raises production.
scenes.visual: Basin B's GOLD P arrow glows; a label appears: 'limiting nutrient: adding it alone raises production'. Basin A stays clear beside it for contrast.
scenes.narration: So in that lake, with nitrogen and carbon plentiful, phosphorus limited the algae. A nutrient is limiting when adding it on its own raises production.

scenes.tts: Lake two-twenty-seven was fertilised with both nitrogen and phosphorus for years. Then the nitrogen fertiliser stopped. The phosphorus kept coming.
scenes.caption: Lake 227 was fertilised with both nitrogen and phosphorus for years. Then the nitrogen fertiliser stopped. The phosphorus kept coming.
scenes.visual: Lake 227 from above, green, ringed by the GOLD dashed line. Two BLUE inputs, TEAL N and GOLD P. A timeline bar runs along the bottom; at '1990' a pair of scissors cuts the TEAL N arrow. The GOLD P arrow continues.
scenes.narration: Lake 227 was fertilised with both nitrogen and phosphorus for years. Then the nitrogen fertiliser stopped. The phosphorus kept coming.

scenes.tts: With its nitrogen input cut, you might expect the algae to fade. They did not. Cyanobacteria that fix nitrogen took over. They fixed nitrogen from the air, an input that kept coming after the fertiliser stopped. Its rate can still respond to phosphorus supply and other conditions.
scenes.visual: Chains of cartoon cyanobacteria (beaded strands labelled 'nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria') spread across the surface. The BLUE sky arrow carrying TEAL N, labelled 'fixation (an input)', thickens.
scenes.narration: With its nitrogen input cut, you might expect the algae to fade. They did not. Cyanobacteria that fix nitrogen took over. They fixed nitrogen from the air, an input that kept coming after the fertiliser stopped. Its rate can still respond to phosphorus supply and other conditions.

scenes.tts: The lake stayed highly eutrophic, year after year. Algae stayed as abundant as the phosphorus allowed. Fixation had made up the missing nitrogen.
scenes.caption: The lake stayed highly eutrophic, year after year. Algae stayed as abundant as the phosphorus allowed. Fixation had made up the missing nitrogen.
scenes.visual: Timeline runs on to '2005'; the lake stays green the whole way. Beside it, a GOLD P input gauge and a green algae gauge move together (schematic). Citation tag 'Schindler and colleagues, PNAS, 2008'.
scenes.narration: The lake stayed highly eutrophic, year after year. Algae stayed as abundant as the phosphorus allowed. Fixation had made up the missing nitrogen.

scenes.tts: These are small lakes in Ontario, and one lake is not a replicate. Other lakes, and many estuaries, can respond to nitrogen. And production is often co-limited, rising only when both nutrients are added together.
scenes.visual: Zoom out: Lakes 226 and 227 shrink to two dots among many lakes and an estuary cartoon, each with a '?' tag. Label 'two lakes, not all waters'.
scenes.narration: These are small lakes in Ontario, and one lake is not a replicate. Other lakes, and many estuaries, can respond to nitrogen. And production is often co-limited, rising only when both nutrients are added together.

scenes.tts: So in these lakes, phosphorus supply set how much algae the lake could hold. Fixers can make up missing nitrogen. No microbe can fix phosphorus.
scenes.visual: Return to the lake ringed by the GOLD line: GOLD P enters by the BLUE input arrows only; TEAL N enters by the inputs and by the fixation arrow from the sky. Labels: 'P inputs: inflow, dust, fertiliser; no fixation' and 'N inputs: those routes + fixation'.
scenes.narration: So in these lakes, phosphorus supply set how much algae the lake could hold. Fixers can make up missing nitrogen. No microbe can fix phosphorus.

scenes.visual: Hex end card with one line: 'Fixers can make up missing nitrogen; no microbe can fix phosphorus.'
